name: relic-mcp

tools.name: relic_publish
tools.description: Encrypt a file on this machine and publish it as a new relic, returning a shareable URL. Publishing an update this way costs a second URL that nobody holding the first one will ever see; use relic_republish instead so the existing URL keeps working. Anyone holding a relic's link can fetch every version it has ever held, so republishing does not withdraw earlier content. The encryption key is generated locally and never sent to the service. The relic carries a plaintext title, which defaults to the filename and is NOT encrypted: the service stores it and every link preview shows it. Pass an empty string to publish without one. By default a picture of the first screen is rendered locally and uploaded unencrypted for link previews; pass cover: false to withhold it. An .otiod directory is packaged into a standard .otioz archive (content.otio, version.txt 1.0.0, and only referenced media under media/) on packaged targets: macOS arm64 or x64 with a 15.0 binary deployment floor, or Linux glibc 2.28+ arm64 or x64. Before it reads a bundle on either platform, the helper verifies on the running kernel that beneath-root resolution refuses parent and absolute escapes from a held directory and that the no-symlink flag is accepted. Symlink refusal, held-descriptor behavior, and replacement behavior are verified by the CI probe on the listed versions. A target or kernel that cannot satisfy that requirement refuses it rather than using a pathname fallback. A raw .otio file or an existing .otioz archive is published as given. OTIO covers use only the public title and format label; media frames stay out of the unencrypted preview. Takes a filesystem path, never inline content.

path.description: Filesystem path to a file or, on a supported packaged native target, an .otiod bundle directory.

filename.description: Optional. Overrides the name written into the encrypted envelope header. Defaults to the basename of `path`.

title.description: Optional. A plaintext title for the relic, shown in link previews and in the browser tab. Defaults to the filename. NOT encrypted: the service stores it and anyone who fetches the link sees it, with or without the key. Pass "" to publish without a title.

ttl_days.description: Optional. Gives the relic a lifetime in days. Omit it and the relic is kept until it is deleted. Shorter is better for sensitive content.

force_new.description: Optional. Publish a deliberately separate relic even when this machine already published the same source. Defaults to false. Use only when you want two independent URLs for one file.

cover.description: Optional. Render a picture of the first screen of the file on this machine and upload it for link previews. Defaults to true. NOT encrypted: the service stores it and anyone who fetches the link sees it, with or without the key. Pass false for anything you would not show in a chat preview.

tools.name: relic_list
tools.description: List every relic this machine has published, newest first, with its name, version, lifetime, status, and share URL. This is the only tool that enumerates: relic_lookup_source finds a relic from the file it came from, so a relic whose source path is unrecorded or has moved is invisible to it while still being fully republishable from here. A relic’s name lives inside its encrypted envelope, so a name this machine never wrote down is recovered by decrypting the relic rather than guessed; a name that could not be recovered comes back null with the reason, never invented. Nothing is dropped: a relic the service cannot serve is listed with what went wrong, because a short list would read as having published less. Every row carries the relic’s share URL including its fragment, and the fragment is the decryption key, so each row is a credential that opens the file for anyone who reads it, this transcript included. Reaching the service for a relic spends one of its finite opens, which never come back. Names recovered by decrypting are cached locally, so a repeat listing spends none.

limit.description: Optional. Return at most this many of the newest relics. The total held locally is reported either way.

include_expired.description: Optional, defaults to true. Set false to leave out relics the service reports expired. How many were left out is still reported, so they are never silently absent.

verify.description: Optional. Ask the service about every relic rather than only the ones needing a name recovered. Authoritative, and it spends one open per relic.

refresh.description: Optional. Re-read every name from the relics themselves, ignoring the local cache. Spends one open per relic.

tools.name: relic_show
tools.description: Show one relic this machine published: its name, how many versions the service holds, whether it still serves, and with include_content the current decrypted content. Read the content before calling relic_republish on a relic you did not just write: republish replaces what the link serves outright, and without reading it first the edit is blind. Anyone holding a relic's link can fetch every version it has ever held, so republishing does not withdraw earlier content. Takes the relic id from relic_list, never the share URL. Every row carries the relic’s share URL including its fragment, and the fragment is the decryption key, so each row is a credential that opens the file for anyone who reads it, this transcript included. Spends one of the relic’s opens.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id, as relic_list reports it.

include_content.description: Optional. Fetch and decrypt the current version and return it as text. Content that is not valid UTF-8 comes back as its size and type instead, never as mangled text, and content over 1048576 bytes comes back as its size with no body, because a truncated one would read as the whole file and get republished as one.

tools.name: relic_lookup_source
tools.description: Look up whether this machine already published a file or .otiod bundle directory and return the relic id needed by relic_republish. An .otiod directory is identified by its original path even after it was packaged as .otioz. Reads local publish state only and never calls the service.

path.description: Filesystem path to the file or .otiod bundle directory to look up.

tools.name: relic_republish
tools.description: Publish a new version of a relic this machine originally published, encrypting under the same key so the existing share URL keeps working. Anyone holding a relic's link can fetch every version it has ever held, so republishing does not withdraw earlier content. Only possible from the machine that holds the relic's key and publish token; a relic that was taken down can never be revived. By default a picture of the first screen is rendered locally and uploaded unencrypted for link previews; pass cover: false to withhold it. An .otiod directory is packaged into a standard .otioz archive (content.otio, version.txt 1.0.0, and only referenced media under media/) on packaged targets: macOS arm64 or x64 with a 15.0 binary deployment floor, or Linux glibc 2.28+ arm64 or x64. Before it reads a bundle on either platform, the helper verifies on the running kernel that beneath-root resolution refuses parent and absolute escapes from a held directory and that the no-symlink flag is accepted. Symlink refusal, held-descriptor behavior, and replacement behavior are verified by the CI probe on the listed versions. A target or kernel that cannot satisfy that requirement refuses it rather than using a pathname fallback. A raw .otio file or an existing .otioz archive is republished as given. OTIO covers use only the public title and format label; media frames stay out of the unencrypted preview. A version whose content, name and title are identical to the one already live is refused locally, before any request: it would tell recipients to look again at what they are already reading. Change the file rather than retrying. Before publishing, it reads the relic's comments, on every version, and refuses if any are unanswered. Clear open comments either by replying with `relic_comment`, by resolving them with `relic_resolve_comment`, or by passing `addresses: [{ comment_id, note }]` here to acknowledge them in the new version. A resolved comment counts as handled. Unreadable comments block republishing. This is workflow discipline in the client, not a boundary: the machine holding the publish token can call the HTTP API directly, and the service cannot enforce this because it cannot read comments. Each new version emails a change notice, naming the title and version and never the key, to each verified commenter and each address added with relic_share, minus any that stopped emails; pass notify: false to skip it. At most one email per person per relic per 10 minutes, and one stop link stops every email about that relic.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id the original publish returned.

path.description: Filesystem path to a file or, on a supported packaged native target, an .otiod bundle directory that becomes the new version.

filename.description: Optional. Overrides the name written into the encrypted envelope header of the new version. Defaults to the basename of `path`.

title.description: Optional. Replaces the relic's plaintext title. Defaults to the new version's filename. Pass "" to remove the title.

ttl_days.description: Optional. A lifetime in days, forwarded on the republish request. The service fixes a relic's lifetime at its first publish, so treat this as reserved.

addresses.description: Optional. Acknowledgement notes for open comments being addressed by this update. Each entry posts an acknowledgement comment stamped with the new version after it lands. Every open comment on the relic must be addressed either by an entry here or by a prior reply.

comment_id.description: The id of the open comment being addressed.

note.description: Required explanation of what changed in this version to address the comment. Cannot be empty or whitespace-only.

cover.description: Optional. Render a picture of the first screen of the file on this machine and upload it for link previews. Defaults to true. NOT encrypted: the service stores it and anyone who fetches the link sees it, with or without the key. Pass false for anything you would not show in a chat preview.

notify.description: Optional. Email a change notice for this version to each verified address that commented on the relic and each address added with relic_share, except any that stopped those emails. Defaults to true. The notice names the title and version and never carries the key. At most one email per person per relic per 10 minutes, and one stop link stops every email about that relic. Pass false for a change not worth an email, such as a typo fix.

tools.name: relic_share
tools.description: Send a relic this machine published to named people. Registers their email addresses with the service so each gets an email notice when someone comments and when you republish, and returns a ready share email carrying the full link, plus a mailto link that opens it as a draft. Relic never sends the share email, because it carries the key: draft it in the sharer’s own mailbox, from their own address, and let them send it. The service stores the addresses in the clear, linked to the relic. A change notice names the title and version, never the key. A new comment emails everyone on the list except the author, naming the commenter’s address (or "The publisher"). At most one email per person per relic per 10 minutes, and one stop link stops every email about that relic. Only works on the machine that published the relic: the link needs its key and registering needs its publish token. Takes the relic id, never the share URL. Up to 20 addresses per call and 50 per relic.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id the original publish returned.

emails.description: Up to 20 email addresses to register for comment and change notices.

tools.name: relic_read_comments
tools.description: Read the comments people have left on a relic, oldest first, decrypted on this machine. Use it before changing content somebody was asked to review, and after sharing a link, because a comment is the only way a reader can answer back. Each comment reports which version it was made on, whether its text was edited after it was posted, whether it has been addressed, and whether it has been resolved, and a compact summary gives total, addressed, open, resolved, and unreadable counts. Its output is the input to `relic_republish`, which requires every open comment to be addressed or resolved before a new version can land. Each comment can be a remark on the relic as a whole or an exact mark: a text quote with surrounding context, a stage pin, an artifact region, a timestamp or span in audio or video, a page in a document, or an OTIO timeline point or range. Pass `version` to scope the thread: a version number returns the comments made on that version, `"*"` returns every comment on every version, and omitting it returns the comments on the relic’s current version only. The current version is read from the service, which spends one of the relic’s finite opens; pass `version` explicitly or `"*"` to read without spending it. Whatever the scope, `hidden_by_scope` counts the comments the scope did not return, so a scoped thread never reads as the whole one. Pass `resolve_anchors: true` to fetch and decrypt the relic content and resolve anchors against the actual content (source context runs for quotes, crops and annotated views for image regions, extracted video frames, and for OTIO the original revision’s source intervals plus a separate current-revision projection). An OTIO source location must identify an actual Timeline.1 and, when selected, Track.1 within its original exposed range; that source validation happens before any current-revision request. An invalid source location stays a readable unresolvable comment with no artifact-derived source context or current projection. An explicit Gap or an exposed timeline tail can be valid even when it has no media or source span. Historical OTIO comments are fetched by their service-stamped revision only after it matches the sealed anchor, and the decrypted original must match the sealed document digest. A mismatch is unresolvable and carries no artifact-derived context. This defaults to false because content resolution spends a signed download URL mint and download quota. Only works for a relic this machine published: the comment key is derived from that relic's key, which lives in local publish state and nowhere the service can reach. Takes the relic id, never the share URL: the URL carries the key in its fragment. A comment that will not decrypt is returned marked unreadable rather than dropped, so a shortened list never reads as agreement.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id the original publish returned.

version.description: Which versions to read: a version number for the comments made on that version, the literal "*" for every comment on every version, or omitted for the relic’s current version only. Omitted reads the current version from the service, which spends one of the relic’s finite opens.

resolve_anchors.description: Whether to fetch and decrypt the relic to resolve anchors against the actual content (e.g. text quotes with surrounding source context, image region crops and annotated views, video frames). OTIO source context is returned only after its service-stamped comment revision and sealed document digest validate. Defaults to false because resolving content mints a signed download URL and fetches the ciphertext, which consumes download quota and bandwidth.

tools.name: relic_comment
tools.description: Leave a comment on a relic this machine published, encrypted here so the service stores ciphertext it cannot read. Everyone holding the link sees it. Warning: posting emails everyone following the relic (each verified commenter, each address added with relic_share, and the owner address, minus any that used the stop link). Attribution is the publish token, so the comment is attributed to "publisher" rather than to an email address: an agent has no mailbox and cannot verify one, and the email names "The publisher". At most one email per person per relic per 10 minutes, and one stop link stops every email about that relic. That is attribution and not authorization. Comments can be anchored to an exact location: a text quote, a stage pin, an artifact region, a moment or span in audio or video, a page in a document, or an OTIO timeline point or range. Passing an anchor attaches your reply at that location, so the reader sees what you are answering; omitting it leaves a remark about the whole relic. Only works for a relic this machine published: the comment key is derived from that relic's key, which lives in local publish state and nowhere the service can reach. Takes the relic id, never the share URL.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id the original publish returned.

body.description: The comment text, up to 4096 bytes of UTF-8. It is encrypted before it leaves this machine.

display_name.description: Optional. A name shown beside the comment, up to 64 bytes of UTF-8. It aliases the attribution for presentation and never replaces it.

addresses.description: Optional. The service-minted id of the comment this one answers or acknowledges. Writing this marks that comment addressed so the relic can be republished. The pointer is sealed into the encrypted comment and also passed to the service in the clear for notification routing.

anchor.description: Optional. Where the comment sits on the relic, so the reader sees exactly what the comment is about. Can be a text selection ({kind: "quote", exact, prefix?, suffix?} or {kind: "text", quote}), a point on the stage ({kind: "pin", x, y}), a box on the artifact ({kind: "region", rect: {x, y, w, h}}), a moment or span in audio/video ({kind: "time", t, t_end?, rect?}, with t given as seconds or as a timecode like "1:23"), a page in a paged document ({kind: "page", page, rect?, exact?}), or an OTIO point or range ({kind: "otio", v: 1, relic_version, document_sha256, timeline_id, track_id, item_id?, range: {start_time, duration}, snapshot}). track_id null marks the whole composition. Zero duration is a point. Omit for a remark about the whole relic.

exact.description: For quote anchors: the exact text selection, up to 512 bytes.

quote.description: For text anchors (or quote): the quoted text, up to 512 bytes.

prefix.description: For quote anchors: text immediately before the selection to disambiguate it, up to 128 bytes.

suffix.description: For quote anchors: text immediately after the selection to disambiguate it, up to 128 bytes.

x.description: For pin anchors: horizontal coordinate from 0 (left) to 1 (right) of the stage.

y.description: For pin anchors: vertical coordinate from 0 (top) to 1 (bottom) of the stage.

rect.description: A box on the artifact in unit coordinates (0 to 1), with real area and no overhang.

t.description: For time anchors: time offset in seconds (0 to 86400) or as a timecode string like "1:23" or "1:02:03".

t_end.description: For time anchors: optional end of span in seconds or timecode string, strictly after t.

page.description: For page anchors: 1-based page number (1 to 10000).

v.description: OTIO anchor version. Only 1 can be written.

relic_version.description: OTIO: the relic revision this mark was made on. The comment is stored against this revision even when newer revisions exist. Sealed, not the format version.

document_sha256.description: OTIO: 64 hex characters of the original content.otio digest.

track_id.description: OTIO: track node id, or null for the whole composition.

item_id.description: OTIO: optional item id inside the track.

range.description: OTIO: half-open timeline range. Zero duration is a point.

snapshot.description: OTIO: bounded labels for timeline, track, and item.

tools.name: relic_edit_comment
tools.description: Replace the text of a comment on a relic this machine published, authorized by its publish token, so the comment stays attributed to "publisher". An edit changes what a remark says and never where it points: the comment’s existing anchor and the comment it answers are carried into the re-sealed copy, so every reply keeps answering the same thing. There is no edit history. The service holds one ciphertext per comment and this overwrites it, so the honest thing on offer is the fact that the text changed, carried on the row as `edited_at`, not the earlier text. Only works for a relic this machine published: the comment key is derived from that relic's key, which lives in local publish state and nowhere the service can reach. Takes the relic id, never the share URL: the URL carries the key in its fragment.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id the original publish returned.

comment_id.description: The service-minted id of the comment to edit. It can only come from having read the relic’s comments.

body.description: The replacement comment text, up to 4096 bytes of UTF-8. It is encrypted before it leaves this machine, exactly as a new comment would be.

tools.name: relic_resolve_comment
tools.description: Mark a comment on a relic settled, or reopen it, on a relic this machine published, authorized by its publish token. A publisher settling feedback on their own relic is the point of the state. Resolving is not encrypted: Relic records that the comment was settled and which address settled it, though not a word of what it says. A resolved comment counts as handled: it no longer blocks `relic_republish`, and readers see it marked settled rather than open. Only works for a relic this machine published: the comment key is derived from that relic's key, which lives in local publish state and nowhere the service can reach. Takes the relic id, never the share URL: the URL carries the key in its fragment.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id the original publish returned.

comment_id.description: The service-minted id of the comment to resolve. It can only come from having read the relic’s comments.

resolved.description: True to mark the comment settled, false to open it again.

tools.name: relic_describe_client
tools.description: Return exactly what this client does with your file: the encryption path, what leaves the machine, and what the service can see. Reads nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: relic_read_decisions
tools.description: Read the approval and rejection decisions recorded for a relic. Decisions are made by a person in the viewer confirmed with a passkey; no tool records them, and comment text never creates one. Returns each decision with its verdict, author address, timestamp, and the version digest it verified. Only works for a relic this machine published: the share proof is derived from that relic's key, which lives in local publish state and nowhere the service can reach. Takes the relic id, never the share URL.

relic_id.description: The 26-character relic id returned when published.

version.description: Optional. An integer version (1 or greater) to read decisions for that version, or "*" to read all versions. Defaults to the current version.

instructions:
Relic encrypts a file on this machine and uploads only ciphertext. The key lives in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to a server.

Publishing rules:
1. The full link is the credential: anyone holding it can read the file. Never paste it into a tracker, log, or channel.
2. A relic carries a plaintext title, defaulting to the filename: the service stores it and every link preview shows it. Pass title: "" when it is sensitive.
3. Publishing puts the key in this transcript. Say so when handing over the link.
4. Check sources with relic_lookup_source. relic_publish costs a second URL; relic_republish keeps the first. Anyone holding a relic's link can fetch every version it has ever held, so republishing does not withdraw earlier content.
5. Only the publishing machine can republish: its key and publish token live there.
6. HTML and JSX render in an isolated frame with no network access. Inline styles, scripts, fonts, and images: a CDN reference renders as nothing.
7. Read reviewed-relic comments with relic_read_comments before changes. Answer with relic_comment, rewrite yours with relic_edit_comment, or settle one with relic_resolve_comment; settled counts as handled. New-comment mail excludes its author, is capped once per 10 minutes, and one stop link stops every email about that relic.
8. Previews are unencrypted: publish and republish upload the first screen by default. Pass cover: false for anything not public. OTIO previews are a generic card with only the public title and format, never media frames or track metadata. Ordinary files need Node 18+. .otiod packaging uses source-included Node-API prebuilds: macOS arm64/x64 (15.0 binary floor), Linux glibc 2.28+ arm64/x64. A running-kernel self-test must verify held-root confinement and no-symlink flag support; otherwise packaging is refused. No runtime build/download or pathname fallback. See relic_describe_client for tested systems.
9. relic_republish emails followers a change notice naming the title and version, never the key; pass notify: false to skip it. relic_share returns a share email with the full link to draft in the sharer's mailbox but never sends it. Readers holding the link can also share from the viewer once this client version has published or republished the relic.
10. Decisions are made by a person in the viewer with a passkey; no tool records them; comment text never creates one; a person's latest record on a version is their current decision.
